```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tseries)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(vars)
library(forecast)

```
```{r}
qd = read.csv("/Users/paridhiagarwal/Downloads/Databusters-main/Quarterly Data.csv")
qd = qd %>% rename('Real_GDP' = 'GDPC1')
```


```{r}
missing_info <- colSums(is.na(qd))  # Count missing values per column
cols_with_many_nas <- names(missing_info[missing_info > 90])  # Get column names with more than 90 missing vals
```

```{r}
# We remove the columns with more than 90 missing vals
qd <- qd %>%
  select(-all_of(cols_with_many_nas))

# We remove the first two rows since they contain unneccesary information
qd = qd %>% slice(-(1:2))
```

```{r}
# Adding GDP Grwoth variable here
qd <- qd %>%
  mutate(GDP_growth = (Real_GDP - lag(Real_GDP)) / lag(Real_GDP) * 100)

# Add a binary target variable for contraction (1 if GDP growth < 0)
qd <- qd %>%
  mutate(contraction = ifelse(GDP_growth < 0, 1, 0))
```

```{r}
qd %>%
  select(GDP_growth, contraction) %>%  # Select only the specified columns
  slice_head(n = 15)  # Display the first 15 rows
```

```{r}
# Replace NA values with median of the respective column
df_clean <- qd %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.na(.), median(., na.rm = TRUE), .)))
```

```{r}

#Time series analysis
ts_gdp = df_clean %>% select(sasdate, Real_GDP, GDP_growth)

# Convert 'sasdate' from character to Date format
ts_gdp$sasdate <- as.Date(ts_gdp$sasdate, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
# Convert Date to Year-Quarter format
ts_gdp$year_quarter <- paste0(year(ts_gdp$sasdate), "-Q", quarter(ts_gdp$sasdate))

print(ts_gdp$year_quarter)
```

```{r}
# Ensure that GDP growth rate is numeric
ts_gdp$GDP_growth=as.numeric(ts_gdp$GDP_growth)

# Convert to time series object
ts_gdp = ts(ts_gdp$GDP_growth, start = c(1959,3), frequency = 4)

#Plot the time series
plot(ts_gdp)
```

```{r}
# ARIMA model

fit = auto.arima(ts_gdp)


# Step 1: Fit the ARIMA model to the historical data
fit <- auto.arima(ts_gdp)

# Step 2: Forecast the GDP growth for the next 5 quarters 
forecast_arima <- forecast(fit, h=5)  # h=5 to forecast the next 5 quarters

# Step 3: Extract the forecasted values and confidence intervals
forecast_values <- forecast_arima$mean       # Point forecast (predicted GDP growth)
conf_int_80_lower <- forecast_arima$lower[, 1]  # Lo 80 (80% confidence interval lower bound)
conf_int_80_upper <- forecast_arima$upper[, 1]  # Hi 80 (80% confidence interval upper bound)
conf_int_95_lower <- forecast_arima$lower[, 2]  # Lo 95 (95% confidence interval lower bound)

conf_int_95_upper <- forecast_arima$upper[, 2]  # Hi 95 (95% confidence interval upper bound)



#Step 5: Display the results for the quarters of interest (Q1 2025, Q2 2025, Q4 2025)
contraction_results <- data.frame(
  Quarter = c("Q4 2024", "Q1 2025", "Q2 2025", "Q3 2025", "Q4 2025"),  #Added Q1 2026 for the 4th forecasted quarter
  Point_Forecast = forecast_values,
  Lo_80 = conf_int_80_lower,
  Hi_80 = conf_int_80_upper,
  Lo_95 = conf_int_95_lower,
  Hi_95 = conf_int_95_upper)


#Print the results for the quarters of interest
print(contraction_results)

# Plot the forecast with confidence intervals
autoplot(forecast_arima) +
  ggtitle("ARIMA Forecast of GDP Growth with Confidence Intervals") +
  xlab("Year-Quarter") +
  ylab("GDP Growth Rate") +
  theme_minimal()

```


```{r}
#var model
ts_gdp_var = df_clean[,c('sasdate', 'CNCFx', 'GDP_growth')]
ts_gdp_var = ts_gdp_var%>% rename('Real Disposable Business Income' = 'CNCFx')

# Convert 'sasdate' from character to Date format
ts_gdp_var$sasdate <- as.Date(ts_gdp_var$sasdate, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

# Convert Date to Year-Quarter format
ts_gdp_var$sasdate <- as.yearqtr(ts_gdp_var$sasdate)

# Convert the "Year-Quarter" column to a time series format
ts_gdp$sasdate <- as.yearqtr(ts_gdp_var$sasdate, format = "%Y Q%q")
.
# Convert to a time series object
ts_gdp_xts <- ts_gdp_var[ , c("GDP_growth", "Real Disposable Business Income")]

# Convert to time-series matrix
ts_gdp_xts <- ts(ts_gdp_xts, start = c(1959, 3), frequency = 4)  # Quarterly data

#finding optimal lag
VARselect(ts_gdp_xts, lag.max = 8, type = "const")

optimal_lag <- 2


#fitting var model
var_model <- VAR(ts_gdp_xts, p = optimal_lag, type = "const")

#forecasting
forecast_var <- predict(var_model, n.ahead = 5)


#looking at forecasted values (fcst = forecasted gdp growth for each quarter)
gdp_forecast <- forecast_var$fcst$GDP_growth
print(gdp_forecast)
```

```{r}
# We work with df_clean again to conduct Principal Component Analysis
quarterly_gdp_numeric <- df_clean[, sapply(df_clean, is.numeric)]
# Drop 'Real_GDP' column
quarterly_gdp_numeric <- quarterly_gdp_numeric %>%
  #select(-Real_GDP) %>%
  select(names(adf_results))

# Standardize the remaining columns
quarterly_gdp_standardized <- scale(quarterly_gdp_numeric)

# Perform PCA on the standardized data
pca_result <- prcomp(quarterly_gdp_standardized)
pca_result

```

```{r}
# Get the standard deviations (sqrt of the eigenvalues) for each principal component
explained_variance <- pca_result$sdev^2

# Get the index of the principal component that explains the most variance
most_varied_pc_index <- which.max(explained_variance)

# Get the name of the principal component that explains the most variance
most_varied_pc_name <- paste("PC", most_varied_pc_index, sep = "")

# Print the results
cat("The principal component that explains the most variance is:", most_varied_pc_name, "\n")
cat("The variance explained by this PC is:", explained_variance[most_varied_pc_index], "\n")

# You can also view the proportion of variance explained by this PC
explained_proportion <- explained_variance[most_varied_pc_index] / sum(explained_variance)
print(explained_proportion)

# Print the proportion of variance explained by each PC
#cat("Proportion of variance explained by each PC:\n")
#print(explained_proportion)

```

```{r}
# If 'Real_GDP' was removed, add it back temporarily to the dataset for correlation analysis
quarterly_gdp_numeric <- cbind(quarterly_gdp_numeric, Real_GDP = df_clean$Real_GDP)

# Standardize the data again with 'Real_GDP' included
quarterly_gdp_standardized <- scale(quarterly_gdp_numeric)

# Perform PCA again with 'Real_GDP' included
pca_result <- prcomp(quarterly_gdp_standardized)

# Get the loadings matrix (pca_result$rotation)
loadings <- pca_result$rotation

# Get the correlation of Real_GDP with each principal component
pc_correlation <- cor(quarterly_gdp_numeric$Real_GDP, pca_result$x)

# Print the correlations between Real_GDP and principal components
print(pc_correlation)

# Identify the principal components most related to Real_GDP
most_correlated_pc <- which.max(abs(pc_correlation))
print(paste("Principal Component most correlated with Real_GDP:", most_correlated_pc))

```

```{r}
# Step 1: Select only numeric columns from df_clean
df_clean_numeric <- df_clean[, sapply(df_clean, is.numeric)]

# Step 2: Create the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix <- cor(df_clean_numeric, use = "complete.obs")

# Step 3: Print the correlation matrix
print(correlation_matrix)


# Melt the correlation matrix into long format for easier plotting
correlation_melted <- melt(correlation_matrix)

# Create a heatmap of the correlation matrix
ggplot(correlation_melted, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", midpoint = 0) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Correlation Matrix Heatmap", x = "Variables", y = "Variables", fill = "Correlation")

```
```{r}
# Assuming adf_results contains the names of stationary columns

# Step 1: Filter the df_clean to only include stationary columns
stationary_data <- df_clean[, adf_results]

# Step 2: Perform further analysis (e.g., PCA, regression, etc.) with the stationary variables
# Example: PCA analysis
stationary_data_numeric <- stationary_data[, sapply(stationary_data, is.numeric)]  # Ensure we're working with numeric data
stationary_data_standardized <- scale(stationary_data_numeric)  # Standardize the data for PCA

# Perform PCA
pca_result <- prcomp(stationary_data_standardized)

# View PCA summary
summary(pca_result)
```
